source.title: Understanding Generalization in Diffusion Distillation via Probability Flow Distance
source.authors: Huijie Zhang; Zi-Jian Huang; Si-Yi Chen; Jinfan Zhou; Ze-Kai Zhang; Peng Wang; Qing Qu

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies scaling of diffusion-distillation generalization and calls its result analogous to language-model scaling laws, but it does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, fit the claimed power laws, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports diffusion-model PFD memorization and generalization trends over model size and training-set size. These are related scaling results, but they are not held-out language-model loss or the power-law and compute-allocation measures specified by the claim versions. The paper cites Kaplan et al.; cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures diffusion-distillation memorization/generalization error (PFD) against N/sqrt(|θ|); it fits no power law to loss, makes no extrapolation, no compute allocation, and no downstream evaluation. It only invokes Kaplan et al. as an analogy. The PFD transition curve is a different construct (a memorization-to-generalization transition, not a power-law loss decline), so no version is tested; the finding goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that PFD is a valid, efficient generalization metric. Using it, they report that diffusion distillation shows a memorization-to-generalization transition governed by N/sqrt(|θ|), which they call analogous to LM scaling laws. They also report epoch-wise double descent and early learning, and a bias-variance U-shape in model size.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains diffusion-model students on samples generated by a teacher and measures probability-flow distance. It does not use the language-model loss and run-scaling measurements of the cited original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The descriptor affects how much generalization-error differences appear across architectures: DINOv2 differentiates architectures more than SSCD, while pixel-space values are nearly identical across architectures when N≥2^15. The paper also reports that the DINOv2 generalization-error curve at N=65536 is relatively flat rather than showing the SSCD double-descent rise.

fits_no_version.finding: PFD memorization and generalization error curves across U-Net sizes (0.9M–55.7M on CIFAR-10; 124M/296M on ImageNet) are reported as near-identical when plotted against N/sqrt(|θ|).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion distillation, the memorization-to-generalization transition is governed by the ratio of training-set size to the square root of parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: At about 43–44M parameters, UViT shows higher PFD errors than U-Net for N≤2^15 but lower generalization error at N=2^16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture inductive bias shifts the diffusion memorization-to-generalization transition at fixed parameter count, depending on data size.

record.problems: The scaling findings use PFD errors rather than held-out language-model loss. The main scaling curves are presented in figures without reported fitted exponents or uncertainty estimates in the text. The distillation data are generated by teacher models.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-architecture curve values and other PFD experiments were not extracted as separate rows because the text describes them primarily through figures and they do not measure any claim version. Relevant scaling-family results are retained as aggregate rows.

untested.parts: No held-out LM pretraining loss or power-law fit in N, D or C.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No loss at fixed parameter count across depth/width; the U-Net vs UViT comparison uses PFD.
Image diffusion models are studied, but there is no power-law fit of loss or error. The authors note that train/test denoising loss does not trend consistently with N.
No exponents or fitting-choice sensitivity. The descriptor dependence concerns the PFD metric, not scaling-law fits.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's 'scaling behavior' is a curve-collapse of a transition, not a power law in loss; no exponents are fitted. The appendix shows train/test denoising losses do not decrease consistently with N, but that is a dataset-size effect within the memorization regime, not a test of V5. The study cites Kaplan only as an analogy.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss or parameter/token/compute power-law fit.
No tests of predictions from power laws fitted on smaller language-model runs.
No fixed-compute language-model sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
The architecture comparison measures diffusion-model PFD errors, not loss at fixed parameter count as specified.
Although the study examines image diffusion models and reports scaling behavior in distillation, it does not test whether the same power-law form holds for a loss measure.
No language-model scaling exponents, compute-optimal split, or sensitivity of those fitted quantities to setup or fitting choices is tested.

rows.subject: U-Net-1 through U-Net-10
rows.stage_stated: student models trained by diffusion distillation
rows.operation_detail: Varied student model size and distillation dataset size; measured PFD memorization and generalization errors.
rows.measure: PFD memorization error and PFD generalization error
rows.note: The text reports that both errors show near-identical MtoG transition curves across model sizes when plotted against N/√|θ|. This is a diffusion-distillation generalization result, not a language-model loss power law.
rows.check: State 'observed' should not be set against a claim version; PFD curve collapse is not a power-law loss result. The value is figure only.

rows.subject: U-Net-11 and U-Net-12
rows.stage_stated: student models trained by diffusion distillation
rows.operation_detail: Varied distillation dataset size and evaluated PFD memorization and generalization errors.
rows.measure: PFD memorization error and PFD generalization error
rows.note: The authors describe a consistent quantitative scaling behavior on ImageNet. The reported measure is PFD error, not language-model held-out loss.
rows.check: Same as R1: ImageNet PFD curves, figure only, no power-law fit, no claim-version measure.

rows.subject: U-Net-9
rows.stage_stated: student model trained by diffusion distillation
rows.operation_detail: Compared PFD errors across dataset sizes with a similarly sized UViT.
rows.measure: PFD memorization error and PFD generalization error
rows.value: U-Net has lower memorization error for N=2^6 to 2^10 and lower generalization error for N=2^11 to 2^15; at N=2^16, UViT has lower generalization error
rows.note: The text reports these comparisons but they concern PFD generalization and memorization errors, not loss at fixed parameter count.
rows.check: U-Net vs UViT PFD comparison at a similar parameter count. This is an architecture-family comparison of a non-loss measure, not V4's depth/width shape test.

rows.subject: UViT
